criteria.question: Is the documented NYHA functional class II or III?

criteria.question: Is there a documented myocardial infarction that occurred at least 40 days before the planned ICD implant?
criteria.evidence_hint: MI date (STEMI/NSTEMI, 'history of MI') compared with the planned implant date.

criteria.text: left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or less
criteria.question: Is the documented left ventricular ejection fraction 35% or less?
criteria.evidence_hint: Echo, nuclear or MRI report: 'LVEF 25%', 'EF 30-35%'.

criteria.text: NYHA functional Class I symptoms
criteria.question: Is the documented NYHA functional class I?
criteria.evidence_hint: 'NYHA class I', 'asymptomatic heart failure'.

criteria.text: left ventricular ejection fraction of 30% or less
criteria.question: Is the documented left ventricular ejection fraction 30% or less?

criteria.text: Nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy
criteria.question: Does the chart document nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy?
criteria.evidence_hint: 'nonischemic cardiomyopathy', NICM, 'dilated cardiomyopathy', I42.0/I42.8/I42.9; normal coronaries.

criteria.text: after reversible causes have been excluded
criteria.question: Have reversible causes of the cardiomyopathy been excluded?
criteria.evidence_hint: Work-up ruling out ischemia, tachycardia-mediated, thyroid, alcohol, myocarditis, peripartum, toxins.

criteria.text: the response to optimal medical therapy has been adequately determined
criteria.question: Has the patient been on optimal (guideline-directed) medical therapy long enough that the response has been adequately determined?

criteria.text: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

criteria.text: history of premature HCM-related sudden death in 1 or more first-degree relatives younger than 50 years

criteria.text: left ventricular hypertrophy greater than 30 mm

exclusions.text: The use of the ICD is considered experimental or investigational in primary prevention members who do not meet the above criteria or have had ANY of the following:
an acute myocardial infarction (i.e., less than 40 days before ICD treatment);
NYHA Class IV congestive heart failure (unless member is eligible to receive a combination cardiac resynchronization therapy ICD device);

a cardiac revascularization procedure in the past 3 months (coronary artery bypass graft [CABG] or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty [PTCA]) or are candidates for a cardiac revascularization procedure;
noncardiac disease that would be associated with life expectancy less than 1 year.
The use of the ICD for secondary prevention is considered experimental or investigational for members who do not meet the criteria for secondary prevention.
The use of the ICD is considered experimental or investigational for all other indications in pediatric members.
The use of a subcutaneous ICD is considered experimental or investigational for individuals who do not meet the criteria outlined above.
The use of cardiac contractility modulation therapy is considered experimental or investigational for all indications.

notes: Built from the PDF only (pdftotext -layout). The download holds a single clean copy of the guideline (no redline); position statement revised 05/15/26, reviewed 04/23/26, original effective date 12/15/13. effective_date holds the Revised date, reviewed_date the Reviewed date.

Structure: the document prints 'adults who meet ONE of the following criteria' over six numbered primary-prevention items and one secondary-prevention bullet, then 'children who meet ANY of the following criteria' over ten bullets. Each numbered item / bullet is its own pathway (one pathway per indication). Each adult pathway starts with the leaf 'adults' and each pediatric pathway with the leaf 'children' because the two sections grant different indications and a chart documents age; the document gives no numeric age boundary, so neither leaf has a threshold.

Adult primary-prevention exclusions ('experimental or investigational in primary prevention members who ... have had ANY of the following') are placed inside each of the six primary-prevention pathways as not(any(...)), nested as printed. The NYHA Class IV bullet carries a waiver '(unless member is eligible to receive a combination cardiac resynchronization therapy ICD device)', modelled as all(NYHA Class IV, not(eligible for CRT-D)) inside that any; logically identical to any(not(NYHA IV), CRT-D eligible) outside it. The revascularization bullet holds two alternatives (procedure in the past 3 months; candidate for a procedure) and is split into two leaves of the same any. These exclusions are not applied to the secondary-prevention pathway or to the pediatric pathways, which the document does not subject to them.

The parenthetical definitions under 'Primary Prevention (... who have not yet experienced life-threatening VT or VF)' and 'Secondary Prevention (... who have experienced a potentially life-threatening episode of near sudden cardiac death)' describe the two categories and are not modelled as leaves; a patient with prior life-threatening VT/VF qualifies through the secondary-prevention pathway.

Primary prevention item 1 and item 2 share the leaves 'Ischemic cardiomyopathy' and 'a history of myocardial infarction at least 40 days before ICD treatment' (identical wording in both items); the LVEF thresholds differ (35% or less with NYHA II/III; 30% or less with NYHA I). NYHA Class II or Class III has no threshold object because the schema's enum thresholds express a single comparison, not a set {II, III}; NYHA Class I and Class IV use enum eq.

Time thresholds: 'at least 40 days' / 'less than 40 days' before ICD treatment are number thresholds in days (not duration_months, which the app computes from note dates for treatment trials); 'in the past 3 months' is duration_months lt 3; 'life expectancy less than 1 year' is a number threshold in years.

Item 3 (nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy): 'after reversible causes have been excluded' and 'the response to optimal medical therapy has been adequately determined' are two leaves. The same phrase 'after reversible causes have been excluded' appears in the pediatric cardiac-arrest and congenital heart disease bullets; there it is a separate criterion (reversible causes of the arrest, not of the cardiomyopathy). The secondary-prevention wording 'after reversible causes (eg, acute ischemia) have been excluded' is a third, separate leaf.

Item 4 (HCM): '1 or more major risk factors' is any() of the four parenthetical risk factors; 'judged to be at high risk ... by a physician experienced in the care of members with HCM' is kept answerable because the physician's risk judgment is charted, although the physician's experience is a credential a chart may not show.

Items 5 and 6 share the leaf 'considered to be at high risk for sudden cardiac death' (identical wording). The channelopathy list 'ONE of the following' is any() of four diagnoses. 'Brugada syndrome', 'catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia', 'hypertrophic cardiomyopathy' and 'nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy' are shared between the adult and pediatric sections where the wording is identical (case aside); adult 'congenital long QT syndrome' and pediatric 'long QT syndrome' are separate leaves because the adult wording adds 'congenital'.

Secondary prevention: the single bullet holds two requirements, the life-threatening event associated with ventricular arrhythmic events and the exclusion of reversible causes; both leaves are required.

Pediatric bullets: 'survivors of sudden cardiac arrest' is one shared leaf across six bullets; 'have documented spontaneous sustained ventricular tachycardia' is shared by the Brugada and HCM bullets, while the arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy ('not hemodynamically tolerated') and nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy ('not due to completely reversible causes') bullets qualify the VT differently and have their own leaves. 'in combination with beta-blockers' (long QT survivor bullet) is modelled as a requirement that the patient is on beta-blocker therapy. The last bullet's 'symptomatic, sustained ventricular tachycardia in association with congenital heart disease' is one leaf (the diagnosis is inseparable from the arrhythmia as printed) plus the evaluation leaf.

Subcutaneous ICD: 'meet the criteria for ICD implantation for primary or secondary prevention' for 'adults or children' is modelled by nesting every adult and pediatric ICD pathway inside an any() in the S-ICD pathway, followed by the three bulleted S-ICD requirements (ALL). The contraindication bullet lists three alternatives ('one or more of the following'), the third of which has two parts (explant for a complication; ongoing need). 'Have no indication for antibradycardia pacing' and 'Do not have ventricular arrhythmias that are known or anticipated to respond to antitachycardia pacing' are kept as leaves worded as printed (a nurse asks the chart for the negative statement) rather than not() of the positive condition.

ICD replacement: the Note after the S-ICD section ('Replacement of an ICD meets the definition of medical necessity for device/lead malfunction, change in member's medical condition, battery depletion, or generator end-of-life') is its own pathway, any() of the four reasons, applying to both transvenous and subcutaneous devices.

Code-to-pathway mapping (the document ties no code to a section): codes that describe inserting a transvenous ICD system, generator or lead, or EP testing of a transvenous system (33216, 33217, 33225, 33230, 33231, 33240, 33249, 93640, 93641, 93642, G0448) are governed by every adult and pediatric ICD indication pathway and by the replacement pathway (their descriptors read 'insertion or replacement' / 'with existing leads' / 'at time of initial implantation or replacement'). Subcutaneous system codes (33270, 33271, 93644) and S-ICD programming/interrogation (93260, 93261) are governed by the subcutaneous ICD pathway and by the replacement pathway. Repair, repositioning, removal, lead extraction, pocket revision and LV-lead upgrade of an existing system (33215, 33218, 33220, 33223, 33224, 33241, 33243, 33244, 33262, 33263, 33264, 33272, 33273) are governed only by the replacement pathway, since the document states no criteria for them other than the replacement Note. No covered code is left without a pathway. CCM codes are governed by no pathway: they are investigational and stop at the code gate.

CRT-D: the document addresses 'ICDs alone' and names cardiac resynchronization only in the NYHA IV waiver; G0448 (ICD system with LV pacing electrode), 33224 and 33225 (LV pacing electrode) are in the code table without a tag and are treated as covered ICD codes governed by the ICD criteria. Criteria for the resynchronization component are not in this document.
Wearable cardioverter-defibrillators are not addressed here; the document refers them to Related Guideline 01-93000-30.

All codes in the code table are covered unless printed '(Investigational)': the 30 cardiac contractility modulation / CCM-defibrillation Category III codes (0408T-0418T, 0915T-0931T, 0948T, 0949T) and HCPCS K1030 are investigational and are the cpt of the CCM exclusion. The four primary-prevention exclusion bullets are listed as exclusions as well as modelled in the trees.

Left out as not requirements: the Description section and 'Summary and Analysis of Evidence'; every 'The evidence is insufficient ...' sentence; the LOINC documentation table; the ICD-10 list (recorded in scope.icd10); the NYHA definitions table; the step-therapy protocol exemption paragraph (no step therapy requirement in this guideline); the disclaimer paragraph.
Program exceptions: FEP follows FEP guidelines, SAO follows SAO guidelines, and Medicare Advantage products follow NCD 20.4 Implantable Automatic Defibrillators; recorded in excluded_plans.
